samples.summary: New agent skill ships with no `safety`/`tools` frontmatter, so the documented confirm/dry-run gate for its destructive `slides set-content` path is absent
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/skills/SKILL.md:9-12` states the convention: "Every skill has YAML frontmatter with `name`, `description`, `safety`, and `tools` fields" with safety levels `read-only` / `write` / `destructive`, and SKILL.md:63 tells agents to "Read frontmatter to understand safety level and available tools" and (SKILL.md:67) "For write operations, run with `--dry-run` first". Every sibling skill honours this — e.g. `packages/cli/skills/slides-manage.md:1-11` carries `safety: destructive` plus an explicit `tools:` allow-list. The new `packages/cli/skills/slides-author.md` starts at line 1 with `# Skill: authoring native Wafflebase slides` — no frontmatter at all — yet its main path (lines 11-12 and the "CLI form" section) is `wafflebase slides create` + `wafflebase slides set-content <doc-id> --file deck.json`, a whole-deck destructive content replace against a live workspace, and it also tells the agent to shell out to `soffice --headless`. Vector: an agent loads this skill, finds no `safety` classification and no `tools` allow-list, and therefore applies no confirmation/dry-run before overwriting an existing deck's entire content — the exact control the repo's own convention exists to enforce. It is also missing from the Slides Skills index table (SKILL.md:36-43), so it is discoverable by file only. Nothing in CI validates skill frontmatter: I found no loader, schema or test over `packages/cli/skills/**` (only charter globs in `scripts/agent/charters/charters.json:24,103,143`), so this will not be caught mechanically.
searchedFor: Read packages/cli/skills/SKILL.md in full (conventions + index tables)
Read packages/cli/skills/slides-manage.md:1-25 to confirm the frontmatter convention is real
Read packages/cli/skills/slides-author.md:1-15 to confirm no frontmatter block
Glob packages/cli/skills/* to enumerate sibling skills
Grep for 'skills' across **/*.{ts,js,json,yml,yaml} looking for a frontmatter validator, loader or test — found only charters.json globs and prose references

samples.summary: Seeded slide content is written straight into Yorkie without running the v1 content validators, and the new decor helpers build elements through `unknown` casts that remove the type system as the remaining check
samples.evidence: `writeContent` (seed-templates.ts:86-95) calls `writeSlidesRoot` directly; unlike `PUT /documents/:id/content` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:197 → `assertValidSlidesBody`), nothing validates the payload at seed time. The only place the validators run is the jest spec (`packages/backend/src/template/seed/catalog.spec.ts:67-78`). This change widens what that unvalidated path carries: `shapeEl()` (builders.ts:190-206) returns `unknown`, and `decorate()` splices the result in with a double cast — `...(under as unknown as typeof slide.elements)` (builders.ts:307-310) — while `recolor()` (builders.ts:209-223) writes inline styles through `as unknown as Array<Record<string, unknown>>`. So neither `tsc` nor a runtime assertion constrains the element shapes that a seed run persists into a live deployment's public template; a malformed `data.kind` or `fill` would reach every viewer and exporter of a public gallery card. I confirmed the *current* catalogue is covered by the spec and that role-shaped inline colours are a legitimate stored shape (packages/slides/src/model/placeholder-blocks.ts:32), so this is a missing-guard/hardening observation rather than a live defect: the guard is a test, not the write path.
searchedFor: Read packages/backend/src/template/seed/catalog.spec.ts to see which validators run and over what
Grep for kind: 'role' across packages/slides/src to confirm role colours are a supported stored shape

samples.summary: Newly exported `BUILT_IN_THEMES` is a mutable shared array, and `themedDeck` embeds the shared theme object by reference into every seeded deck
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/node.ts:133-134` now re-exports `BUILT_IN_THEMES` / `getBuiltInTheme`. `BUILT_IN_THEMES` is declared `export const BUILT_IN_THEMES: Theme[]` (packages/slides/src/themes/index.ts:38) — a mutable array of mutable theme objects — and `getBuiltInTheme` (themes/index.ts:49-51) returns the shared instance, which `themedDeck` then stores directly as `themes: [resolvedTheme]` (builders.ts:380) alongside `layouts: BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` (builders.ts:382). Any Node consumer of the new export that mutates a returned theme (or a caller that mutates a deck's `themes[0]` in place) corrupts the registry process-wide, for every other deck built in the same process. I verified the seed path itself is safe today — `applyLayoutToSlide` deep-clones placeholder specs via `clone()` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:434, model/clone.ts:8), so `decorate()`'s `t.frame.x = nx` mutation (builders.ts:299-302) does not reach `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` — so this is latent shared-mutable-global exposure, not an exploited one. Freezing the registry, or returning a clone from `getBuiltInTheme`, would close it.
searchedFor: Grep 'export function clone|const clone =' in packages/slides/src (JSON deep clone)

verdict.reason: The file-level observation is accurate (slides-author.md:1 has no frontmatter and is missing from the SKILL.md:36-43 index), but the security claim — that the confirm/dry-run gate for the destructive `slides set-content` path is absent — is refuted by a concrete counterexample. The safety classification for that exact command exists machine-readably at packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:330-332 (`name: 'slides.set-content'`, `safety: 'destructive'`), and registry.ts:4-7 states this is the field skill agents read to decide when extra confirmation is needed. packages/cli/src/commands/schema.ts:43,58 emits that entry for `wafflebase schema slides.set-content`, and schema.ts:60-63 includes `safety` in the list form; SKILL.md:64 routes agents to `wafflebase schema <command>`, and slides-author.md:69 itself points at `slides set-content --help`, so the classification is reachable without frontmatter. The dry-run gate is implemented in code as a global flag honoured by this command at packages/cli/src/commands/content-write.ts:134-142, independent of any per-skill `tools:` allow-list. Separately, nothing in the repo consumes skill frontmatter at all: grepping the tree for frontmatter parsers and for readers of packages/cli/skills/** found only prose (packages/cli/README.md:249-253) and charter doc-scope globs (scripts/agent/charters/charters.json:24,103,143) that scripts/agent/hunt-corpus.mjs:111-113 deliberately skips. Missing frontmatter therefore weakens no enforced permission gate, crosses no trust boundary and exposes no secret — enforcement is backend authz on PUT /documents/:id/content (content-write.ts:22-31), untouched. The gap is a real docs-consistency issue for the correctness/documentation lens, not a Security-lane defect.
